about.imageAlt: Official WARDOGS gameplay view from a helicopter cockpit
about.bodyOne: WARDOGS is BULKHEAD's upcoming tactical all-out warfare FPS, not the 2016 War Dogs movie. Up to 100 players in three teams contest a randomized 2 x 2 km Control Zone using infantry, vehicles, fortifications, and logistics.
about.bodyTwo: Cash persists between matches and funds a new loadout for each life. Combat and support actions can both help the team while sustaining your economy.

editorial.metaTitle: WARDOGS Wiki Editorial Policy and Research Standards
editorial.metaDescription: See how WARDOGS Wiki verifies official claims, analyzes creator footage, labels build-sensitive details, corrects errors, and keeps every player guide current.
editorial.title: How We Research WARDOGS
editorial.intro: WARDOGS Wiki is an independent fan publication. Every guide is built to answer a player question clearly while separating official facts, observed footage, community reports, and unresolved claims.
editorial.teamBody: The WARDOGS Wiki Editorial Team maintains this focused game guide without affiliation to BULKHEAD, Team17, Steam, creators, or advertisers. Commercial relationships do not determine our conclusions or source labels.
editorial.officialBody: Release dates, prices, platforms, access rules, and feature claims are checked against Steam, Team17, BULKHEAD, or official WARDOGS channels before publication.
editorial.footageTitle: Footage is evidence, not final documentation
editorial.footageBody: Creator videos help explain controls, match flow, loadouts, vehicles, and tactics. Alpha and beta numbers remain labeled build-sensitive unless a current official source confirms them.
editorial.statusTitle: Confirmed and uncertain claims stay separate
editorial.statusBody: We mark rumors, community observations, and unknown details plainly. A missing answer is never converted into a confident release promise or final balance claim.
editorial.updatesTitle: Material updates earn a new date
editorial.updatesBody: Last-checked dates change when sources or guidance are meaningfully reviewed. Pages are not redated merely to appear fresh in search results.
editorial.correctionsTitle: Corrections remain part of the record
editorial.correctionsBody: When a source changes or an error is found, we update the affected guide, revise its status language, and preserve links that let readers verify the current conclusion.
